name: triangle
summary: Draws a CSS triangle out of borders, pointing in a given direction.

arguments.name: $direction
accepts: top
top-right
right
bottom-right
bottom
bottom-left
left
top-left
inline-start, inline-end, block-start or block-end, which follow the writing direction
read in any case, so TOP and Inline-End work

arguments.name: $color
accepts: a Sass colour, such as red, #333 or oklch(70% 0.1 200)
currentColor
a system colour such as Canvas
var(), color-mix(), light-dark(), contrast-color() or rgb(from ...), which CSS resolves
a CSS-wide keyword is refused, because it is invalid inside the border-color shorthand
one colour, not a list: a second would colour a second border and the shape would stop being a triangle
a colour with no alpha is refused, since the border is the whole of the shape

arguments.name: $size
accepts: one length, or two lengths as width then height
var(), env() or a calculation in place of any length
more than two lengths is refused, since only the first two are read

caveats: The colour goes into the `border-color` shorthand, so a list of two coloured a second side: rendered in Chrome 152, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6.2, `triangle("bottom", red blue)` drew a red triangle with a teal wedge beside it in all three. One colour only, since 4.0.0.

The border is the whole of the shape, since the element is 0 by 0, so a colour that paints nothing draws nothing: a transparent triangle was an empty box in all three. A colour with no alpha raises since 4.0.0. A zero size is left alone: it draws nothing too, but it is a coherent resting state for a caret that grows.
Only the first two lengths of `$size` are read, and a third used to be dropped without a word, so `10px 8px 6px` drew the same triangle as `10px 8px`. It raises since 4.0.0.
